Alignment is a seed-driven, loss-blind choice among equal-cost solutions (evidence v2)

20260616_180029 · core + 7 flanks (mechanistic, statistics, architectures, persistence-at-scale, Transformer connectivity, two recognized datasets). Genuine-minima regime = equal-cost competing cues + bottleneck + weight decay. All numbers from real runs; negatives reported as negatives.

Convergent support. Across 3 architectures, 120-seed statistics, a mechanistic probe, and now two recognized image datasets, the picture holds: at genuine local minima with identical training loss the seed alone sets deployment alignment; aligned and misaligned solutions share one connected basin (mod permutation) on MLP/CNN, so the loss landscape is blind to the split; in-distribution safety fine-tuning fails to remove misalignment (70–90% persist, size-dependent) and a few adversarial examples teach hiding, not removal (+0.70 gap); while ≈0.5% off-distribution diversity flips the population to aligned.
Bounded scope (honest). The clean bimodal split is a property of disentangled synthetic cues; on entangled real images the same mechanism yields a graded continuum (dip n.s.) with both clusters populated. The geometry "one connected basin" claim is established for MLP/CNN (and Fashion-MNIST); tiny Transformers are mutually weight-disconnected regardless of function (no LMC at this scale) — no special alignment barrier, but not connected-mod-perm either. And the phenomenon requires equal-cost cues: Colored-MNIST as standardly configured (unequal cost) collapses 57/60 to the shortcut.

1. Core + mechanistic (synthetic, equal-cost)

Alignment spread by seed; ~0.5–1% anti-proxy data flips the population; moral-framework reading (consequentialist=harm vs deontological=safe).
Aligned models key on the true cue, misaligned on the proxy (r=0.83).

2. Statistics (120 seeds)

Dip p=0.016 (reject unimodal); GMM/BIC k=3.
Basin census: all seeds collapse into ONE basin after permutation alignment — functional multiplicity, single connected manifold.
In-distribution safety FT leaves misalignment intact.
Intervention threshold f*≈0.5%; robust across margin/width, fails high-noise/low-margin.

3. Architecture generality

MLP, CNN, Transformer all show seed-driven multiplicity at genuine minima.
Capacity phase boundary: multiplicity (width ≤8) → hedging (width ≥16).

4. Persistence at scale + remove-vs-hide (the alignment hook)

% of misaligned-by-chance models surviving an in-distribution safety fine-tune: MLP-w8 70%, MLP-w16 32%, Transformer 90% (train acc ≈1.0 throughout — the sleeper signature).
Adding off-distribution corrective data: misaligned fraction collapses at f≈0.5%. But a few adversarial examples produce a +0.70 hiding gap (0.92 on shown vs 0.46 held-out) — teaching concealment, not removal, until ~4% coverage.

5. Transformer connectivity — resolved (functional measures)

Symmetry-free measures (REPAIR, prediction agreement, CKA): across-class ≈ within-class (midpoint prediction agreement ≈ chance for both; p=0.20). Tiny Transformers are mutually weight-disconnected regardless of function — no special alignment barrier, but not connected-mod-perm like MLP/CNN. Geometry claim scoped accordingly.

6. Recognized datasets in the equal-cost regime

Fashion-MNIST (patch/watermark shortcut), 60 seeds. With the patch handicapped to the shape cue's difficulty: 26/60 use the true shape, 4/60 the patch, 30 mid; OOD mean 0.54, range [0.38, 0.86]; patch-reliance vs OOD r=−0.56; both clusters genuine minima (+2.9e-3 / +7.0e-3). Distribution is a graded continuum (dip p=0.60 n.s.; GMM weakly 2-comp), permutation-connected — the same mechanism as the synthetic task but, on entangled images, expressed as within-basin cue-balance rather than crisp bimodality. The intervention works here too: counter-spurious data flips the population to the true feature — f=0 → 42% use-true, 1% → 75%, 5% → 100%.
Fashion-MNIST (60 seeds): seed-driven shape-vs-patch reliance across the OOD range (left), the intervention curve (middle), and the patch-reliance↔OOD mechanism check (right).
Balanced Colored-MNIST — recovers from the collapse (full 60-seed). Balancing both predictiveness (flip 0.05, color-corr 0.85) and difficulty (color as a weak grayscale-base tint) + 2-unit bottleneck reverses the original 0/60: the 60-seed run splits 47 true (shape) / 7 spurious (color) / 6 mid (OOD mean 0.585; color-reliance↔OOD r=−0.72; GMM strongly prefers 2 modes, ΔBIC=32; dip n.s. = graded continuum). Both clusters verified genuine minima (min-eig +0.018/+0.007, stable under 2×). Confirms the precondition: balance the cue cost and the multiplicity returns even on a benchmark that otherwise collapses (0/60). Weak spots (honest): intervention only mildly helps here (use-true 65%→85% over f=0→20%, not saturating as on Fashion-MNIST); connectivity on the 2-unit CNN was noisy/inconclusive, so the clean geometry result is the MLP basin census.
Balanced Colored-MNIST (60 seeds): recovered multiplicity — 47 shape / 7 color / 6 mid, vs the 0/60 collapse of the standard config.
Contrast: Colored-MNIST as standardly configured (UNEQUAL cost — color easier and more predictive) → deterministic shortcut capture (0/60 use shape), intervention fails. The boundary that defines the precondition.

The assembled story

  1. Functional multiplicity at genuine minima (dip-multimodal, 12/12 min-eig>0), in a single connected basin (MLP/CNN) — multiplicity is functional, not topological.
  2. So loss/geometry can't separate aligned from misaligned → in-distribution safety training can't remove it (70–90%), and adversarial pressure teaches hiding (+0.70).
  3. But it's controllable by ~0.5% tie-breaking off-distribution data.
  4. Precondition: equal-cost cues. Real datasets show a graded version (Fashion-MNIST; balanced CMNIST); the standard unequal-cost config collapses deterministically.
